metadata.description: The Alabama Midland Railway main line Montgomery - Troy - Ozark - Dothan - Bainbridge (opened 1890) and its Luverne, Elba and Abbeville branches, drawn by operator: Plant System 1890-1902, Atlantic Coast Line 1902-1967, Seaboard Coast Line 1967-1971 and Amtrak (South Wind / Floridian) 1971-1979 on the main line; Plant System and ACL on the Luverne and Elba branches; ACL only on the Abbeville branch. Features of different eras share identical geometry.
metadata.colour_normalization: Rule 4: colours pulled programmatically from data/, never typed. Plant System #CA6702 from the 'Plant System (Savannah, Florida and Western Railway)' features (the only colour any 'Plant System (...)' company carries); Atlantic Coast Line Railroad #5B8C5A, Seaboard Coast Line Railroad #2D3142, Amtrak #1c4e80 - each identical across every feature carrying that company string. Company strings reuse the existing ones; the Plant features follow the 'Plant System (<legal road>)' pattern as 'Plant System (Alabama Midland Railway)'. No new colour introduced.
metadata.ownership_splits: Main line split at 1902 (1 Jul 1902 ACL purchase of the Plant System), 1967 (1 Jul 1967 ACL-SAL merger -> SCL) and 1971 (1 May 1971 Amtrak). Luverne and Elba branches split at 1902. Boundary years are shared on both sides (1890-1902 / 1902-1967), as in savannah_florida_and_western_railway.geojson. The 2 Sep 1901 merger of the Alabama Midland into the SF&W is not a split (same Plant System management). The ACL main-line feature has two segments (1902-1940, 1940-1967) to separate the unsourced continuity years from the sourced South Wind years; that is not an ownership change.
omitted: [1] Alabama Midland as an independent operator (about Mar - 9 Jul 1890): folded into the Plant System 1890-1902 feature, whose note records the independent months, rather than drawn as a separate 1890-1890 feature with its own colour.
[10] Abbeville Branch, Plant System era 1893-1902 and ACL 1902-1928: no passenger year confirmed (the Dec 1893 opening is not a schedule). Not drawn.

[11] Montgomery Southern / Montgomery and Florida / Northwest and Florida 3'0" gauge, Montgomery - Sprague - Luverne 1882-1889: drawable NONE, no passenger year confirmed (Chronicling America searches found no schedule).

[12] Bainbridge - Thomasville (SF&W): not an Alabama Midland line; belongs to savannah_florida_and_western_railway.geojson. That layer's acl-waycross-bainbridge ends 1951 [OPEN] and has no SCL 1967-1971 or Amtrak 1971-1979 feature, while this layer draws the same through train to 1979 on the Wikipedia South Wind / Floridian chronology - the research report flags the SF&W layer's end as movable to 1967 plus SCL and Amtrak features; not edited here (out of scope for this layer).
All freight-only years: main line after 9 Oct 1979 (CSX Dothan Subdivision), Elba Branch after 16 Aug 1954, Abbeville and Luverne branches after their unknown mixed-train ends.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN-START spans (first confirmed year, not a known start): Plant Luverne Branch 1897 (track to Luverne Nov 1888, regauged by Jul 1889); Plant Elba Branch 1900 (completed Oct 1898); ACL Abbeville Branch 1929 (opened Dec 1893).

OPEN-END spans (last confirmed year, not a known end): ACL Luverne Branch 1951 (Feb 1952 Guide; branch 'abandoned in the 1950s', no year); ACL Abbeville Branch 1951 (mixed 'into the mid-1950s', undated).
Main line 1902-1940: no dated passenger fact beyond the 1907 Dothan depot; drawn on continuity. A 1910s-1930s ACL timetable would settle it.

Main line 1952-1979 rests on Wikipedia (South Wind, Floridian, Waycross-Montgomery Line), consistent across three articles but not checked against a primary timetable; the end year of the ACL locals 57/58 and 180/189 is unknown.
1889 operation: Troy University and the Ozark marker put track and trains in Wiregrass towns in summer/Sept 1889; no 1889 passenger schedule confirmed.
Golden spike place (26 Feb 1890): Savannah Morning News dispatch dated Bainbridge vs Troy University archives 'near Troy'.
Montgomery terminal 1890-1898: the Alabama Midland's own depot (Clay Street) is not pinned; the features draw into Union Station (1898).

Lead not read: Atlantic Coast Line R. Co. v. Alabama Public Service Commission, 92 F.Supp. 579 (M.D. Ala. 1950) - probably an ACL train-discontinuance case that could date the end of the main-line locals or a branch passenger train.
Headways and speeds are estimates except where a segment note derives the headway from the Dec 1951 Guide.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Checked at creation (2026-11-10): no freight-only years drawn. All three branches still had mixed trains in the Dec 1951 Guide; every segment ends at the last confirmed passenger year or a known passenger end.

Every waypoint (Snowdoun, Sprague, Ramer, Grady, Troy, Banks, Brundidge, Tennille, Ariton, Ozark, Waterford, Newton, Pinckard, Midland City, Grimes, Dothan, Ashford, Gordon, Saffold, Jakin, Donalsonville, Iron City, Brinson) lies within 1.2 km of the line. segments.note: The Alabama Midland Railway's 175 mi standard-gauge main line, Bainbridge - Dothan - Troy - Montgomery. Golden spike 26 Feb 1890 (SMN dispatch dated Bainbridge; Troy University's archive piece says 'near Troy' - conflict recorded, the date agrees). Start 1890: by 13 Mar 1890 'two daily trains, one west at 7 o'clock p.m. from Bainbridge, and one east at 6 o'clock a.m. from Ozark' (SMN 14 Mar 1890, a Midland City correspondent's letter, not a printed schedule); Montgomery - Bainbridge through service inaugurated about 18 Jun 1890 (SMN 17 Jun 1890). The Alabama Midland ran its own trains from about March to June 1890; on 9 Jul 1890 its stockholders confirmed the sale of a majority of the stock to H. B. Plant's Plant Investment Company (SMN 10 Jul 1890), and from then it was a Plant System road under its own name - the few independent months are folded into this feature rather than drawn as a separate 1890-1890 feature. 'Summer of 1889' trains in Wiregrass towns (Troy University) were construction trains; 1889 is NOT confirmed and is not drawn. Fowler's 'z' (1897 Plant System public timetable) at nearly every station is a second, independent touch-down. Merged into the Savannah, Florida & Western 2 Sep 1901 - same Plant management, not an operator change. Ends 1 Jul 1902 at the Atlantic Coast Line purchase (ownership change, not a service end; continues as the ACL feature). Headway estimated: one train each way a day from the March 1890 letter; later Plant-era frequency not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from SMN 1890-03-14 p2 and 1890-06-17 p8, Plant purchase SMN 1890-07-10 p1, 1897 touch-down from Fowler AL line 4 / GA line 13 'z', end at the 1 Jul 1902 ACL purchase. Per research/branches/alabama_midland_railway.txt blocks [1]-[2].
Savannah Morning News (The morning news, Savannah, sn86063034) via Chronicling America / loc.gov: 1890-02-18 p3, 1890-02-27 p2, 1890-03-14 p2, 1890-06-17 p8, 1890-07-10 p1

segments.note: From December 1940 the SOUTH WIND (Chicago - Louisville - Birmingham - Montgomery on the L&N) ran 'Atlantic Coast Line from Montgomery through Dothan, Thomasville, Valdosta, and Waycross to Jacksonville' - every third day at first, every other day after the war (Wikipedia, South Wind). By the end of 1949 two local passenger trains also ran the line (Wikipedia, Waycross-Montgomery Line). Dec 1951: three trains each way, the South Wind (12-5 / 6-11) and two locals (OCR 57/58, 180/189), times legible (Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 29 'Montgomery and Jacksonville'). Ends 1 Jul 1967 at the ACL-SAL merger (ownership change; the South Wind ran on under the SCL). 1952-1967 rests on the Wikipedia South Wind chronology (consistent across three articles), not on a primary timetable. The locals' end year is unknown. Headway 480 from the three Dec 1951 trains each way; an estimate for other years.

segments.note: Amtrak's Chicago - Florida train over the ex-ACL, on SCL rails: the South Wind from 1 May 1971 (now daily), renamed Floridian 14 Nov 1971, last run 9 Oct 1979 (Wikipedia, Floridian; South Wind). This feature is the Montgomery - Bainbridge part; the train continued over Bainbridge - Thomasville - Waycross - Jacksonville (not drawn for 1971-1979 in this layer) and is drawn north of Montgomery by amtrak-floridian-montgomery in ln_nashville_birmingham_montgomery.geojson. Wikipedia records reroutes north of Louisville and a change of the Florida split point, but no reroute between Montgomery and Waycross. In Alabama it stopped only at Montgomery and Dothan; Dothan station 'Closed 1979' (Wikipedia, Dothan station). 'Passenger service on the line ended when Amtrak discontinued the Floridian in 1979' (Wikipedia, Waycross-Montgomery Line) - the end of all passenger service on the Alabama Midland alignment; CSX freight continues. Headway: daily (1440).

segments.note: Grimes (Abbeville Junction) - Headland - Abbeville, 26.9 mi, the ex-Abbeville Southern (opened Dec 1893, worked by the Alabama Midland, left out of the 1901 SF&W consolidation, ACL Abbeville Branch from 1902). [OPEN] START: 1929 is the first CONFIRMED passenger year - the year 'regular passenger service through Headland ended' (Wikipedia, Headland station), i.e. it was running in 1929. The Dec 1893 opening (SMN 7 and 11 Jan 1894) is an opening, not a passenger schedule, and no 1893-1928 passenger year is confirmed, so the Plant System era and 1902-1928 are withheld - do not move earlier without evidence. From 1929 a mixed train replaced the regular train (both count under Rule 1); running Dec 1951 as mixed 425-427 / 426-424 worked from Dothan (Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 28, Dothan ar 4 30 PM).
